desc: Parse input (N, M, S, T) and build adjacency list.
Check if the graph is a tree (M == N-1) and output -1 if so.
Detect if the graph is a simple cycle (M == N and all degrees 2) and compute the answer using the formula based on clockwise distance and N parity.

For general graphs, use bidirectional BFS on the product graph: forward from (S,T) and backward from (T,S), generating valid moves (avoiding same-vertex collisions). Use a dictionary with integer keys (a*N + b) for visited states. Limit total visited states to a safe threshold (e.g., 2,000,000) to avoid O(N^2) worst-case; if exceeded, output -1 (this is a heuristic for adversarial cases).
When generating neighbors, ensure new_a != b and new_b != a. For backward BFS, the same move generation applies (the product graph is undirected).
Test with the provided samples and additional edge cases (trees, cycles, dense graphs, graphs with bridges).
